name: as-switching-dynamics
title: The Dynamical Signature of Switching
question: What is the dynamical signature of the agent's action switching — how do its distance-to-resource and internal nutrient states evolve as it alternates?
claim: Distance to A and B are anti-phase and the nutrients sawtooth in step with engagement — the agent rhythmically switches between foraging the two resources.

expected_behavior.name: antiphase-engagement-sawtooth-nutrients
expected_behavior.condition: committed M2 seed, representative config, max_steps 2500
expected_behavior.rationale: Distance-to-A and distance-to-B alternate below the resource radius (anti-phase engagement); each nutrient rises when its resource is engaged and falls otherwise (sawtooth).

findings.summary: ~9-10 alternating engagement cycles; nutrients sawtooth, sustained by switching (slow net decline).
findings.detail: figures/action_switching.png: shaded bands alternate red/green (engaged with A/B) in anti-phase; the nutrient panel shows each level rising on engagement. figures/nutrient_phase.png traces the switching cycle in internal-state space.

config.caption: Anti-phase distance-to-resource traces (shaded = engaged) + sawtooth nutrient levels — the switching signature (cf. Beer Fig. 12).
Video — the CTRNN's activation pattern during switching: node-ring graph (neuron outputs + weights) + a time raster; the sensor and motor neurons modulate as the agent engages each resource.
Nutrient A vs nutrient B over the trial — the switching cycle in internal state.
Video — the switching behaviour in the world.

derived.insight: ~9-10 alternating engagement cycles; nutrients sawtooth, sustained by switching (slow net decline).
